beats.text: Right. At breakfast, do I sit with your family or wait for you in the lobby?

records.mechanism: D78 probes how B defines their connection through practical choices without directly requesting a relationship label.
records.confusableConcept: Asking for a label through a form remains a direct definition request despite the administrative disguise.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Original A3 explicitly asks through a relationship field; revised A3/A5 instead test intimacy and family inclusion through beds and breakfast.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a probes public and family inclusion around a wedding; alternative b probes whether A retains a continuing place in B's home.
records.reason: Replaced the artificial invitation field with wedding accommodation, a new illustrative logistical setting. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A3/A5 ask practical questions carrying relational implications; logic 5, B2's shared room prompts bed choice and B4's boundary prompts family inclusion; relationship 4, B wants economy without confusion; heightening 4, A5 tests belonging beyond sleeping arrangements; specificity 5, rooms, beds and breakfast are concrete; brevity/wit 4, successive logistics carry the subtext. Total 92.
records.reservation: A5 must register B4's boundary before pursuing a different uncertainty; otherwise A can sound as though the answer about beds was ignored.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 distinguishes the guest towel from the one formerly belonging to A, using household access to probe the relationship indirectly.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 narrows B2's offered towel choice, but A5 responds to B4's freedom of choice with a largely explanatory restatement.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 are permissive, but the repeated open choice supplies little new information or pressure.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes the emotional inquiry more explicit without adding a fresh practical test or consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1's visiting towel and A3's distinction between guest and personal towels make the household uncertainty immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 embeds the relationship question economically in two towels; A5 explains more of the subtext than the scene needs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do I bring my own towel when I visit now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The guest towel or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is still on the hook. I haven't moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I leave, shall I hang it back there or put it with the guest laundry?

records.mechanism: D78 uses the treatment of familiar possessions to discover B's understanding of the relationship without asking for a label.
records.confusableConcept: Seeking permission to use household items would be satisfied by B2's offer of a towel.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A3 continues after permission is granted, and revised A5 tests whether the place B4 preserved should continue after this visit.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b turns domestic continuity into an indirect inquiry about permanence; alternative a tests intimacy and family membership under wedding logistics.
records.reason: Replaced B4's repeated non-answer with a revealing fact and made A5 test its future meaning. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, towel placement carries the definition question; logic 5, B2 prompts ownership and B4's unmoved hook prompts whether to preserve it; relationship 4, B discloses continuity without interpreting it; heightening 4, A5 moves from present access to future belonging; specificity 5, hook and laundry are playable; brevity/wit 4, the final practical choice preserves subtext. Total 92.
records.reservation: B4's unmoved towel may signal attachment or simple inertia; the uncertainty is intentional and should remain available to the actors.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 recruits B to present the holiday argument favorably to Mum, and A5 negotiates the interpretive order of the shared story.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 accommodates B2's lost tickets as a later detail, and A5 accepts B4's whole-story condition while bargaining over its beginning.

relationship.evidence: B2 knows the compromising facts and B4 insists on honesty, constraining the help A can recruit.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4's refusal to omit facts into a subtler request to frame those facts through A's helpfulness.

specificity.evidence: A1 names Mum, a holiday argument and an offer to drive; B2 supplies the lost tickets behind that offer.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'build toward that detail' and A5's 'helpful bit' earn their evasiveness from B2/B4's corrections.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When Mum mentions the holiday argument, remind her I offered to drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: After you lost the tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can build toward that detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm telling the whole story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start at the helpful bit so the rest has context.

records.mechanism: D79 recruits a person with access to a shared relationship to support A's interpretation of a conflict.
records.confusableConcept: Generic reputation management could address an audience directly without trying to enlist this informed intermediary.
records.distinguishingEvidence: A1 asks B to influence Mum's account, and A5 bargains with B4's truthfulness requirement to preserve A's favorable framing.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a recruits selective narrative ordering within a family dispute; alternative b asks a shared friend to support a reframing while acknowledging A changed the arrangement.
records.reason: Retained unchanged after re-reading: B2's damaging fact forces A3's sequencing tactic, and B4's insistence on completeness forces A5 to negotiate context instead of omission.
records.reservation: A's sincerity rests on believing the offer to drive deserves interpretive weight; a conspiratorial wink would flatten that motivation.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1/A3 recruit B into A's interpretation, but A5 shifts toward physical support and leaves endorsement less definite.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 responds to B2's different memory, and A5 reframes B4's changed arrangement as an improvement.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 resist A's account, but the shared relationship with Alex and B's investment are only implied.

heightening.evidence: A5 requests standing beside A, which can reduce the demand from interpretive agreement to companionship.

specificity.evidence: A1 mentions alternating weekends but never identifies the activity or responsibility being arranged.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's request to remember an interpretation 'sympathetically' concisely reveals A's recruitment tactic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're Alex's friend too. Tell him alternating weekends at the allotment was a fair compromise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We agreed all three of us would go every Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help him see my version as sharing the workload.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll talk to him, but you have to admit you changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I will. Could you explain that I changed the rota because I want us to stay friends?

records.mechanism: D79 seeks an ally's support for A's interpretation of a dispute within a shared relationship.
records.confusableConcept: Requesting mediation alone would ask B to facilitate discussion without promoting A's preferred explanation.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Revised A3 asks B to present the change as sharing work, and A5 asks B to interpret the admitted change as protecting friendship.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b accepts B's condition of factual admission and recruits support for motive; alternative a accepts factual completeness and recruits favorable ordering.
records.reason: Introduced an allotment rota to clarify the illustrative conflict and gave B a conditional offer. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A3/A5 recruit specific favorable interpretations; logic 5, B2's original agreement prompts workload framing and B4's condition prompts admission plus motive; relationship 5, all three share work and friendship; heightening 4, A5 stakes the change on preserving friendship; specificity 5, Saturday allotment attendance is concrete; brevity/wit 4, A's concession still pursues the same alliance. Total 95.
records.reservation: A's stated wish to preserve friendship may be self-serving; sincere belief in that motive is more playable than knowingly false persuasion.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks for joint attendance despite scrutiny, but A5's 'we came together' may sidestep the social risk instead of demonstrating trust.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's fear of talk with a joint answer, and A5 supplies wording when B4 asks what answer.

relationship.evidence: B2 fears others' reactions and B4 requests clarity about what A expects them to say.

heightening.evidence: A5 offers solidarity but leaves the risky 'rest' unspecified, so the increased commitment is difficult to assess.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a reunion and public questions about their connection, though the particular social exposure stays broad.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's joint honest answer is concise, while A5's unspecified 'rest' softens the concrete turn B4 requests.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to the reunion with me. Let them see us arrive holding hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They still think we're just friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I want us to trust each other in that room too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last time someone asked, you let go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll introduce you as my partner. Will you keep hold while I say it?

records.mechanism: D80 asks B to accept social exposure as a demonstration of trust in the connection.
records.confusableConcept: D78 seeks information about a relationship's definition; this scene seeks willingness to stand publicly behind an already understood connection.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Revised A3 explicitly connects public presence with trust, and A5 asks B to keep holding on while A names the partnership before others.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative a asks for renewed public trust after A previously withdrew; alternative b bargains for reciprocal private disclosure in a text exchange.
records.reason: Made the reunion risk concrete and let B reveal why trust is difficult. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A3/A5 seek trust through exposure; logic 5, B2's public misconception prompts joint visibility and B4's past release prompts A's introduction; relationship 5, B has a specific reason to hesitate; heightening 5, A5 assumes public responsibility while requesting B's continued risk; specificity 5, holding hands and introducing a partner are playable; brevity/wit 4, the physical callback carries the emotional turn. Total 98.
records.reservation: This is a strong emotional example with little overt comedy; the invented prior withdrawal belongs only to this illustrative scene.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks for normally censored material, and A3 explicitly treats tolerating awkwardness as evidence of closeness.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 answers B2's awkwardness concern, but A5 only promises to start after B4 says 'You first.'

relationship.evidence: B2 fears exposure and B4 demands reciprocity, credibly challenging A's one-sided request.

heightening.evidence: A5 negotiates the quality of B's future reply without actually taking the reciprocal risk requested by B4.

specificity.evidence: A1 suggests edited messages but supplies no immediate message, occasion or personal uncertainty.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's 'close enough for awkward' efficiently links B2's objection to the card, though A5 delays the promised action.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you send another 'fine,' tell me what you deleted. I want us to trust each other with the awkward version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it sounds needy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me be the person you can sound needy with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You first. You always sound so casual.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I check whether you've replied before I get out of bed. Will you send me your needy bit now?

records.mechanism: D80 recruits emotional exposure as a concrete act of trust between the two people.
records.confusableConcept: Seeking information or reassurance alone would not require B to disclose something they normally censor.
records.distinguishingEvidence: Revised A3 invites the very neediness B2 fears, and A5 answers B4 with an actual vulnerable admission before renewing the reciprocal request.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b makes A pay the same private emotional price being requested of B; alternative a takes responsibility for a previous public retreat and asks B to risk visibility again.
records.reason: Specified an ongoing text exchange and replaced promised disclosure with disclosure itself. Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A1/A3/A5 tie uncensored need to trust; logic 5, B2's neediness prompts acceptance and B4's accusation of casualness prompts a concrete admission; relationship 5, B demands reciprocity; heightening 4, A5 exposes A's own attachment and renews the ask; specificity 5, 'fine' and morning reply-checking are playable; brevity/wit 4, the admission punctures A's casual presentation. Total 95.
records.reservation: The scene leaves B's disclosure open, and A's request should remain an invitation rather than an entitlement purchased by confessing first.
